chains.title: Candidate TFAP2E binding change near a dELS element
chains.element: A possible regulatory element 42 bp away, EH38E2269392; the variant does not overlap it.

links.claim: If TFAP2E occupies the variant, QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to ref T than alt G. This is an in-vitro prediction without occupancy support. TFAP2A and TFAP2C have the same reported mapped-model change, so the model does not distinguish these related factors; TFAP2E is retained as the candidate because the listed prediction uses its own model and it has the highest reported expression of the three in HCT 116.
A nearby dELS cCRE could be relevant, but it is 42 bp from the variant and its reported activity is a maximum across biosamples, not evidence of activity or a variant effect in HCT 116.
PYDC2 is a proximity-based candidate target, not a demonstrated target of the nearby cCRE or variant; no significant variant eQTL is reported for colon tissues.
HCT 116 is a plausible context because TFAP2E is expressed there, but no variant-overlapping TFAP2E occupancy or regulatory effect is shown.
A TFAP2E–PYDC2 contribution to colorectal cancer is speculative; the supplied evidence reports no variant association and no PYDC2–colorectal-cancer association.

predictions: If this chain is correct, TFAP2E should occupy the variant in relevant cells and show greater binding to ref than alt; perturbing the variant or TFAP2E should affect a linked regulatory readout.
The binding-model result alone does not predict whether PYDC2 expression rises or falls, because stronger TF binding need not mean greater transcriptional activity.
falsified_if: Sensitive assays find no TFAP2E occupancy at the variant in relevant cells, or find no reproducible ref-favored binding.
Perturbing the variant or the proposed element has no effect on a linked regulatory readout or PYDC2 expression.

EBF4 is expressed in HCT 116, but there is no evidence of its occupancy or regulatory action at this site in that cell line.
An EBF4–PYDC2 contribution to colorectal cancer is speculative; the supplied evidence reports no variant association and no PYDC2–colorectal-cancer association.
